item.description:
Fixes for data loss in named volumes, in names that differ only in upper and lower case, and in docker rename. Update the app and the container runtime: brew upgrade --cask containerstack and brew upgrade bshk-app/tap/container@1.7.1 (Apple Container 1.7.1-bshk.2). An app update through the app itself does not update the runtime.

Added

  • Welcome window. It opens after the first install, after an update to a new major version, and after an update that adds a step to it. It shows what ContainerStack adds to Apple Container. One step installs the cstack command in your PATH and, after you agree, the agent skill. Open it again from Help › Welcome to ContainerStack; Help › What's New in ContainerStack shows these notes.
  • Settings in panes. Settings are grouped in a sidebar.
  • Window look. One surface color with thin lines between areas.

Fixed

  • Postgres volumes (0.1.0 to 0.11.0). Creating a container whose environment sets PGDATA (every official postgres image does) on a named volume that held data and still had lost+found replaced the volume with an empty file system. The usual trigger was docker compose up recreating a Postgres service on a volume that another container, the container CLI, or ContainerStack before 0.9.0 had filled. If a database went missing after a compose up, restore it from a backup: the volume no longer holds it.
  • Shared volumes (0.9.0 to 0.11.0). Creating a container on an empty named volume while another container ran on it replaced the volume under the running container, and that container's later writes were lost.
  • Names that differ only in case (all versions). On the macOS default file system, web and Web share one storage folder in Apple Container. A volume create under the second spelling erased the first volume's data; a container create under it, and a later delete, removed the first container's files; a machine create overwrote the first machine's configuration. Apple Container 1.7.1-bshk.2 refuses such a name, and Docker answers 409 "Conflict. The container name … is already in use by container …".
  • docker rename (all versions). Apple Container cannot rename, so ContainerStack deleted the container and created it again: a container that had run lost every file that it wrote outside its volumes and bind mounts, and its logs.
  • A container whose stored state fails to load is kept at the next start of the runtime, not deleted.
  • -v name:/path:nocopy works; before, the container failed to start.
  • cstack <command> --help prints the usage instead of running the command, also when the help flag comes before compose.
  • Container group dividers and the list rows have one style in every resource list.

Changed: what is now refused or only warned

  • A new volume is filled from the image (which also removes lost+found) only after the container was created, only when the volume is empty and clean, and only when no other container uses it, running or not. Otherwise the volume stays as it is, and docker create, docker run and docker compose print a warning that names the volume, says why, and says how to fix it.
  • nocopy (also volume-nocopy=true) is honoured as in Docker: the volume is not filled from that mount.
  • docker rename of a container that has run is refused with an error that says why. Create a new container under the new name from the same image instead, and copy data out of the old one first with docker cp. A container that was created and never started still renames, so docker compose up keeps re-creating services. A container that never ran can still be refused when ContainerStack cannot tell that it never ran: remove it and create it again.
  • A rename to a name that differs from another container's name only in case is refused before anything changes, also when the runtime keeps its data on a case-sensitive volume, where it would have worked.
  • A create that finds a folder left by an interrupted earlier create, with files in it, is refused with the folder's path and how to keep the files (mv it away). An empty folder is reused.

What to do when a volume was not prepared

When another container already uses a new volume, when two services that share one new volume are created at the same time, or when nocopy is set, ContainerStack does not prepare the volume. When the container needs the image's files there, or Postgres refuses to start because of lost+found:

  1. Stop every container that uses the volume.
  2. Copy the files in, or run docker run --rm -v <volume>:/v busybox rmdir /v/lost+found.
  3. Start the container again.

Or start the container that fills the volume first, or point PGDATA at a subdirectory.

Known limitations

  • The rename check runs before the delete. A container started with the container CLI at that moment is not seen and loses its files, as before.
  • A volume is filled from the image only when Apple Container keeps its data in its default folder.
  • When a create is refused because a storage folder that belongs to no container, volume or machine holds files, the message suggests an mv command. That command fails when the folder's path contains an apostrophe or when the name is about 250 characters long. Move the folder away by hand.
  • When a container that has no network exists under a name that differs only in case from buildkit, container build fails with a misleading message. The same is true for container cluster create and a container under the cluster's name in another case. No data is changed.

Shared runtimes: several docker run -i --rm sessions of one group can run in one VM, not one VM for each run. Both groups are off by default.

Added

  • Shared runtimes. Settings > Shared Runtimes has two groups: mcp-catalog (images mcp/*) and stdio-sessions (any plain docker run -i --rm). Turn on a group, then restart the Docker bridge once. Matching runs then start as sessions in one shared VM. See the guide.
  • Containers shows a shared VM as a group with its sessions below it. A session has Stop and Logs. The group has Stop, with a confirmation that shows how many sessions end.
  • The inspector tells why a run did not join a group, for example a TTY, a mount or a published port.
  • Doctor shows whether shared runtimes are on. cstack doctor counts the sessions and counts the memory of each shared VM once.
  • When the bridge runs without shared runtimes, ContainerStack removes the shared containers that an earlier bridge left.

Fixed

  • docker events --until no longer drops events that arrive shortly before the deadline.
  • The DNS server for containers reports the port that it uses. Before, it reported the requested port also when that port was in use.

Known limitations

  • The sessions of one shared container are one trust domain: they run as one user on one writable file system. To keep a run separate, add --label containerstack.group=none.
  • Sessions do not support docker exec or docker cp.

The Docker bridge no longer stops when a client writes input to a container whose program has ended. Stop on a stack keeps its containers. A Homebrew install puts cstack in your PATH.

Added

  • cstack in PATH. The Homebrew cask links the cstack command into the Homebrew prefix.

Fixed

  • The Docker bridge no longer stops when a client writes input to a container whose program has ended, for example yes | docker run -i --rm busybox head -1. Before, this also ended the output of all other containers.
  • Stop on a stack no longer removes its containers and network, so the stack can start again. Remove is a separate action. It removes the containers and the network and keeps the volumes.
  • docker ps -a shows the exit code of a container that was stopped through the Docker API. Before, it showed Exited (-1).
  • docker cp into a container accepts a tar archive whose last file has no padding. Before, the request failed with HTTP 500.
  • Kill events in docker events show Linux signal numbers, as Docker does.
  • When the runtime helper stops, it also stops the Docker bridge. Before, the bridge continued to run.
  • Images and volumes refresh every 60 seconds, so changes made outside the app appear in the lists and on the Overview.
  • Images and Run no longer show the images of the runtime.
  • After Stop, Start, Restart or Remove, the status message names the action. Before, it said "<name> is ready."
  • The inspector keeps your choice after a quick switch between sections.
  • The sidebar no longer moves while the inspector opens in a narrow window.
  • The note under the default container size names cstack doctor as the place of the memory check.

ContainerStack now runs on Apple Container 1.7.1. Settings has the default CPUs and memory of containers and of the image builder, and builders stop when they are idle.

Added

  • Default container resources. Settings has a new section, Default Container Resources. It sets the CPUs and memory of each container that is started with no limit: from Run Container, from Docker API clients such as docker and docker compose, and from the container CLI. The values are saved in Apple Container's config.toml ([container] table), so all three use the same numbers. A change applies to new containers after a restart of the Docker bridge. Before, such a container got 4 CPUs and 1024 MB.
  • Image builder size. Settings > Image Builder sets the CPUs and memory of the image builder ([build] table of the same file). A running builder keeps its size; the new values apply the next time it starts.
  • Builders stop when idle. A builder VM keeps the memory it has used until it stops. ContainerStack now stops a builder that has done no work for the time set in Settings > Image Builder > Stop when idle for: Never, 5, 10, 30 or 60 minutes. The default is 10 minutes. This applies to the Apple image builder and to buildx builder containers. A builder with a running build is not stopped. The build cache stays; the next build starts the builder again.
  • Restart of the Docker bridge only. Restart Docker Bridge in Settings restarts only the Docker API bridge. Apple Container and the running containers stay up.
  • Skill for coding agents. ContainerStack links a containerstack skill into the skill folders of Codex and Claude Code. The skill tells an agent to use docker and docker compose through ContainerStack. Settings > Coding Agents has the switch.

Changed

  • Apple Container 1.7.1. The runtime moves from 1.3.1 to 1.7.1. Existing images, volumes and containers stay. The first container after the update can take about 10 seconds to start.
  • The Doctor's memory check now counts the image builder VM and names its part of the total.

Fixed

  • After an update of the app, the runtime starts when you open ContainerStack. Before, the Docker socket stayed dead until you pressed Start.
  • The first start on a Mac with no default kernel now installs the kernel. Before, the start failed.
  • docker cp into a volume or bind mount of a running container now writes the file where the container sees it. Before, the command returned success and the file was not there.
  • An image push no longer leaves image data in the memory of the runtime.

Known limitations

  • A buildx builder container takes the Default Container Resources when buildx creates it, and keeps that size until it is removed.
  • The idle check runs one time each minute, so a builder stops up to 1 minute after the limit.
  • act --use-new-action-cache gets a 500 error.

The Docker bridge no longer uses CPU all the time while a client waits for a container.

Fixed

  • For each docker run --rm, and for each other client that waits for a container to exit, the bridge read the full container list every 100 ms. It did this for as long as the container ran, also after the client was gone. The bridge now checks one container once per second as a fallback, and stops when the client disconnects.
  • Measured with one waiting client for 30 s: the bridge used 0.30 s of CPU before and 0.04 s after.

Runtime restarts now wait for the previous Docker bridge to exit before continuing.
Doctor shows which restart step is running and clears an old repair warning after a
fresh report confirms that every check passed.

Fixed

  • Stop and Restart wait for the Docker bridge to exit. If it ignores the stop signal,
    ContainerStack ends it after a short grace period. A failed stop is reported instead
    of being treated as successful. The app and cstack use the same behavior.
  • Doctor shows the current restart step and the runtime's error message when available.
  • A fully healthy Doctor report clears a warning from an earlier failed repair, including
    after the runtime was restored outside the app. Incomplete checks and timeouts keep the
    warning visible.

ContainerStack now uses native macOS lists and a separate inspector column. You can move
through the lists with the keyboard. The runtime now runs Start, Stop and Restart one at a
time, in the order of your clicks.

Added

  • Native lists for the sidebar, Containers, Images, Volumes, Networks and Stacks, with the
    system selection color and VoiceOver support. A click on a row gives that list keyboard
    focus, and the arrow keys move the selection.
  • The inspector is a column of its own, with a Hide Inspector button in the toolbar. The
    toolbar buttons of a screen stay over its list.
  • Run… in the toolbar opens the Run Container sheet with a picker of local images. Pull
    stays in Images.
  • Edit in the context menu of a stack row opens the stack editor, also when the inspector
    is hidden.

Fixed

  • Start, Stop and Restart of the runtime run through one queue. The app does the last action
    that you click. A Stop during a Restart now ends the restart. Before, the app lost that Stop.
  • When the app stops the runtime helper, the helper also stops the container system start
    that it began. Before, that start could overlap the next Stop.
  • Stop and Restart of a stack now have a 120-second deadline. Before, a runtime that did not
    answer kept the stack busy and disabled every stack action.
  • A status check on a busy Mac no longer loses the output of the command.
  • In light mode, the inspector buttons and the status pills are readable.
  • Start in the stack inspector is the prominent button only while a service is stopped.
  • Image avatars take their initials from the repository name, not from docker.io. A
    container keeps its avatar color across launches.
  • The port column shows the first mapping and a count, for example 8080→80 +1.
  • A click anywhere on a group header expands or collapses the group.
  • Return in the New Stack sheet creates the stack.
  • Logs open at the newest line. A recent container in Overview opens in Containers.
  • The sidebar says Overview, and the first inspector tab is Info. The menu bar Quit item has
    Command-Q. The volume inspector no longer shows a Used by row that always read "—".

Known limitations

  • Images and volumes that you create outside the app show only after Refresh or a relaunch.
  • Stop on a stack runs docker compose down. It removes the containers and the network of
    the stack. A stack that the app found only from container labels then leaves the list.
  • A second pull of an image whose layers are already on disk can stay at "Pulling…".
  • The inspector has a fixed width of 404 pt. The search field stays over the inspector.

ContainerStack gets a Doctor: the checks cstack doctor runs, now in the sidebar, with a button
for each problem the app can fix itself. Around it, a round of fixes to how the app starts, stops
and watches the runtime.

Added

  • Doctor in the sidebar. It runs when you open it, at most once every 30 seconds, and again
    whenever you ask. Each check shows its verdict, and one with a known fix gets a button: Restart
    Runtime or Repair Docker Context. The window and cstack doctor share one report, so they
    cannot disagree; the CLI's text, flags and exit codes are unchanged.
  • A stopped runtime shows which checks were skipped and why, instead of nothing or a false pass.
  • When another ContainerStack copy's bridge holds the Docker socket — /Applications beside a
    development build, say — Doctor names its path and process, and Restart Runtime replaces it.
    A bridge from any other program is named, never stopped.

Fixed

  • The menu bar keeps tracking the runtime after you close the window. Closing it used to stop
    the 3-second monitor, which froze the status and turned off automatic recovery for as long as
    the app lived in the menu bar alone.
  • Stop stays stopped. A start still under way no longer launches the runtime after you stop it,
    and nothing begun before or during the Stop — a status check, a container stop that fails
    afterwards — restarts it once the Stop is done. A deliberate stop is no longer reported as
    "Runtime helper exited".
  • Start works after a start got stuck. It used to do nothing, without a word, while the helper
    the app had given up on was still running; Start and Restart now end that helper and launch a
    fresh one.
  • Stopping a group of containers or taking a stack down hands a lost runtime connection to
    automatic recovery, as stopping a single container already did. "Checking the runtime…" no
    longer stays on screen once the check is over, and a message on one screen no longer replaces
    another screen's.
  • A runtime that has just recovered no longer goes blank because a check started before the
    recovery came back late.
  • Uninstalling with Homebrew boots out the runtime LaunchAgent, which otherwise kept relaunching
    a helper that was no longer there.
  • Adding a volume onto a container path that already has one from a different source is refused,
    instead of reporting success and changing nothing.

Known limitations

  • Published ports still need a runtime restart if a bridge-created network's vmnet helper dies;
    restarting only the containers does not repair the host route. Doctor now spots it and offers
    the restart.
  • Running an image from the Images screen still waits for the container to exit before it
    returns.
  • A Stop clicked while a restart is in progress, including one the app started on its own, is
    lost.

Fixed

  • runtime: repair a dead docker context record without activating it (737807f)
  • runtime: repair a dead docker context record without activating it (36659bf)
  • runtime: replace the mutation-slot poll with a continuation queue (c8186ba)

Apple Container moves to 1.3.1, which closes six security advisories in the layer
that pulls and unpacks images. Updating the app updates the runtime with it:
brew upgrade --cask containerstack pulls both.

Security

  • The pinned runtime moves from Apple Container 1.2.2 to 1.3.1. All six advisories
    fixed in containerization 0.42.0 covered the 0.40.1 that 1.2.2 carried. Four are
    reached by pulling an image from a registry you do not control; one of those,
    CVE-2026-65388, could hand your registry credentials to whatever host the
    registry names in its authentication challenge — over plain HTTP if it asks, and
    on a login that fails, because the client sends them before it stores them.
    The other two are reached by creating a container and by loading an image layout.
  • The Docker bridge was ported to that runtime. A tarball whose index carries one
    entry the runtime now refuses to read still loads the images beside it, rather
    than failing whole.

Added

  • A runtime this build was not tested against is now stated plainly, naming the
    version found, the version required, and the command that fixes it. Until now the
    helper exited, launchd restarted it every ten seconds, and the app could only say
    the helper had exited — the same sentence it shows when a socket never opens.

Changed

  • Image pushes and registry inspection now always use https. Apple Container 1.3.0
    removed the scheme detection that downgraded internal hosts to plain HTTP, and
    Docker's own default is the same. A registry served over plain HTTP is no longer
    reachable through those two paths.

Known limitations

Published ports still require a runtime restart if a bridge-created network's vmnet
helper dies; restarting only the containers does not repair the host route. Running
an image from the Images screen still waits for the container to exit before it
returns.
